evidence.interaction_completeness: app.js implements shaped skeleton (785-812), load error (814-832), Esc/backdrop blocked while busy (1724-1737), Luhn card validation (1439-1520), simulated provider failure (1548-1565), acknowledgement-gated cancellation (1927-1931) and scheduled-change Undo (1302); test-output/checks.json shows no console or page errors.
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: index.html has a skip link (line 12), header/aside/nav/main landmarks (14-55) and an aria-labelledby dialog (109); the progressbar has min/max/now/text (app.js 474-478); checks.json reports one serious axe target-size violation on 2 nodes at desktop (lines 30-41) and none on mobile.

Invoice 'Download' only fires a toast (app.js 1878-1880), and the 36/36 interaction suite cited in analysis.md has no output artifact in the packet.

critical_defects: The fixed prototype-controls bar overlays the member usage card in screenshots/mobile.png, hiding the '18 of 20 members' line and progress bar, and permanently occupies the bottom of the viewport (styles.css 1879-1891, 2339-2344).

Downgrade/cancellation copy promises the owner will choose which three members keep access, but no member-selection step exists; a downgrade can be scheduled with 18 members while that consequence stays unresolved (app.js 1601-1604; analysis.md 193-194).
Invoice 'Download' is a stub that only shows a toast, so the primary invoice affordance does not deliver a document (app.js 1878-1880).
strengths: One-glance status: plan, price, renewal date and seat usage are adjacent, with cancellation separated yet discoverable through the page nav.
Two-step change review exposes effective date, estimated charge, next payment and seat overflow, and never claims a payment succeeded.
Role model explains restrictions in place instead of showing dead owner controls, while preserving all read-only facts.
Broad state coverage: loading, load error, empty invoices, past due, scheduled change with Undo, validation, provider failure and busy guards.

evidence.product_understanding: analysis.md lines 14-25 labels prices, dates, proration and cancellation policy as synthetic, but the cancellation assumption (line 21: existing 16 members stay on Free) conflicts with the brief's 3-member Free limit (task.md lines 7-11) and with B's own blocked downgrade above 3 members (analysis.md line 78).
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md lines 36-57 orders the page by owner questions, and app.js renderSummary/renderUsage/renderPlans/renderBillingDetails/renderDangerZone (429-755) follows it; however screenshots/mobile.png is 3818 px tall, with three stacked plan cards ahead of Payment and invoices and no in-page navigation.
evidence.design_judgment: analysis.md lines 61-80 documents the strongest decision in either packet: 'Price display' for comparison never changes the active cadence (app.js 540-560 keeps state.data.cadence, visible in desktop.png); trade-offs for the two-step annual change and blocked downgrade are stated.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png uses one dominant summary panel with $29 as the focal figure and an integrated 16/20 usage bar, then plans, payment/invoices and cancellation; tabular numerals and restrained green/amber/red produce a trustworthy document feel. mobile.png keeps the order but runs 3818 px.
evidence.interaction_completeness: app.js covers loading (768-798), load error (800-809), free/payment-issue states, acknowledgement-gated cancellation (1094-1104, 1457-1461), payment validation with first-error focus (1178-1236) and an honestly unresolved failed payment (renderPaymentIssue 368). Gaps: no card-save failure state, and no dialog close guard during the 750 ms save (submitPayment 1227-1262).
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: index.html has a skip link (11) and main landmark (63), app.js exposes a labelled progressbar (521), and checks.json shows no horizontal overflow at 390 px; but axe reports a serious color-contrast violation on 6 nodes at both viewports (checks.json 31-42, 70-81), and the 11.5 px footer uses #85918b on #f4f5f2, about 3.0:1 (styles.css 21, 1321).
evidence.implementation_quality: app.js uses a single state object, render functions and systematic esc() on injected HTML (152-162), with design tokens in styles.css 7-63; both viewports load with zero console/page errors (checks.json). The 71-check suite cited in analysis.md 151-163 has no output artifact in the packet.

critical_defects: Serious axe color-contrast violations on 6 nodes at both desktop and mobile; the footer text is roughly 3.0:1 against the canvas (test-output/checks.json 31-42, 70-81; styles.css 21, 1321).

Cancellation policy contradicts the stated Free plan: a 16-member workspace is told existing members stay on Free, while downgrading to Free at 16 members is blocked (analysis.md 21, 78; app.js 1060-1085).
The blocked downgrade is a dead end: the review says to remove 13 members, but the prototype has no member-management path, so the owner cannot complete the task (analysis.md 179; app.js 927-936).
No dialog cancel/close guard during payment save, so Escape or a close action can dismiss the modal while the save is still running (app.js 1227-1262).
strengths: Best single design decision in either packet: price display is separated from commitment, so browsing annual prices cannot imply a subscription change.
Strong visual system: single summary panel, focal price, tabular numerals, calm palette and a document-like tone suited to billing.
Usage is integrated into the summary with an 80% warning and plain consequence, with the upgrade action adjacent.
Honest unresolved-payment state after a card update; consistent 'no payment was processed' notices and clear plan-delta review rows.
Role restrictions are explained in place, and members still see plan prices for informed discussion.

comparison: Both packets supply comparable evidence: 1280 px desktop and 390 px mobile full-page screenshots, analysis, implementation and DOM/axe output, so visual hierarchy is scoreable. Candidate A is the stronger product and UX artifact: richer state coverage, guarded dialogs, an explicit role matrix, and a clearer mobile task order with in-page navigation. Candidate B is the more polished visual system and has the sharper design insight by separating price display from commitment, but its cancellation policy contradicts the Free-plan limit, axe finds 6 serious contrast failures on both viewports, its blocked downgrade is a dead end, and its mobile page is far longer without in-page navigation. Weighted (15/20/15/15/15/10/10): Candidate A 3.65 of 4, Candidate B 3.30 of 4.
limitations: Only the default owner view was supplied as rendered screenshots (1280 desktop, 390 mobile); dialogs, loading, error, empty, past-due, at-limit and member views were judged from code and analysis, not images. Neither packet includes the interaction-suite output its analysis cites (A 36/36, B 71 checks), so those counts are unverified. Axe findings cover only the rules that ran and are not proof of WCAG conformance, and some of B's flagged nodes may be prototype chrome, though the footer is product surface. No screen-reader, real-device or Firefox/Safari testing was available. In A's full-page mobile capture, fixed prototype chrome overlaps content, so its real scroll behavior cannot be fully judged. This is one blinded pass, not a statistical result or proof of causation.
